blocks.text: FY2026 payroll inquiry responses
HANGS Construction Services LLC
Fiscal year: July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026
Asked by: the audit team, September 14, 2026
Answered by: Dana Whitfield, Controller
Answered on: September 18, 2026
Status: answers in writing, with Renata Salazar, Payroll and HR Manager; not a representation letter
Q1 Headcount and wages. How many people did HGC employ, and why did wages rise from FY2025?

Answer: We averaged 91 people per regular payday in FY2025 and about 96 in FY2026: Alder Point and Tideflats added crews. There was no general raise; five people had individual rate changes effective December 22, 2025.
Q2 The June 26 bonus run. What was the June 26, 2026 bonus payroll?
Answer: Project-completion bonuses of $55,500.00 for 6 superintendents and project managers on Harbor Ridge Commons and the Northgate library, approved by the President and CEO on June 19, 2026.
Q3 Shared deposit account. Two employees are paid into the same bank account. Who are they and why?

Answer: Xavier Baptiste (E-1044) and Alicia Baptiste (E-1051), both journeyman carpenters, are married and asked to be paid into their joint account. Both direct deposit forms are signed and in their personnel files with their I-9s and W-4s, and they work on different jobs under different superintendents.
Q4 Rate approvals. Who approves a pay rate change, and were all the FY2026 changes approved?

Answer: The Chief Financial Officer approves field and estimating rates and the President and CEO approves office salaries, on a signed personnel action form before payroll enters the change. Renata Salazar enters every change. Her own increase to $98,000.00 was agreed in her review with the President and CEO, but the form was not signed before she entered it.
Q5 Leavers. How is someone who leaves removed from payroll?
Answer: The superintendent or manager sends the last day worked; payroll pays the final check on the next regular payday and inactivates the employee the same day. Six people left in FY2026.
Q6 Accrued wages. What is accrued for wages at June 30?

Answer: Wages earned from June 22 to 30 and paid on July 10: seven of the nine working days for hourly crews and seven of ten for salaried staff. Employer payroll taxes are expensed when the payroll is paid, so none is accrued.
Q7 L&I deduction. How does the payroll system work out the L&I employee share?
Answer: On the hours payroll sends to the rate: regular hours plus time and a half for overtime, the same premium hours we use for job costing.
Q8 Forms 941. Were all four Forms 941 filed on time, and was any amended?
Answer: Yes. The payroll system files them and I sign them; none was amended. The payroll system makes the deposits on the semiweekly schedule.
Demonstration document. Every name and figure is invented.

trail.what: Reading FY2026 trial balance.xlsx
trail.result: Read FY2026 trial balance.xlsx: 27 balance sheet and 15 income accounts, two columns each; “FY2026 close complete”.

trail.what: Reading FY2026 payroll expense ledger.xlsx
trail.result: Read FY2026 payroll expense ledger.xlsx: 87 lines for accounts 5110, 6110, 6210 and 2190, July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026.

trail.what: Agree the trial balance and tie the payroll accounts to the payroll expense ledger
trail.result: The trial balance balances at June 30, 2026 with the year’s income accounts in it, and at June 30, 2025 after closing; “FY2026 close complete”. Field wages $9,130,071.59, office salaries $2,927,123.19 and employer Social Security and Medicare $880,857.32 are the ledger’s to the cent, and accrued wages roll from $274,413.75 to $314,193.69 through its two accrual journals.

trail.what: Propose materiality from the year’s revenue, as the audit plan sets it
trail.result: Contract revenue $68,989,500.00 x 0.5% = $344,947.50, rounded down to $340,000.00. Performance materiality $255,000.00; clearly trivial $17,000.00. Payroll and employer taxes are $12,938,052.10, 18.8% of revenue. The engagement shareholder sets the final amounts.

trail.what: Plan the Payroll Audit
trail.result: The trial balance and the payroll ledger agree · wages $12,057,195 · materiality $340,000.00 proposed

trail.what: Reading FY2026 payroll register.xlsx
trail.result: Read FY2026 payroll register.xlsx: 27 payrolls, 2,493 paychecks and 99 people in the employee master, plus the July 10, 2026 payroll.

trail.what: Reading FY2026 payroll inquiry responses.docx
trail.result: Read FY2026 payroll inquiry responses.docx: 8 written answers from Dana Whitfield, September 18, 2026.

trail.what: Agree the register to every paycheck and to the employee master
trail.result: 27 payrolls, 26 biweekly and the June 26 bonus run, paid $12,017,414.84 of gross pay. Each payroll is its paychecks to the cent (2,493 in all), and the 99 people in the employee master were paid the same total. Field wages $9,102,218.35 and office wages $2,915,196.49 add up to it.

trail.what: Set an expectation for each month: its paydays at the year’s average gross per payday, plus any bonus run
trail.result: The year’s average biweekly payroll is $460,073.65. Every month is within 4.4% of its expectation; the largest gap is January 2026, ($40,344.51). October and May have three paydays, the calendar rather than a change in pay, and June has the $55,500.00 bonus run (Q2). Nothing over the 10% threshold.

trail.what: Set an expectation for the year’s wages from headcount and compare it with the books
trail.result: FY2025 wages $11,422,455.58 for an average 91 people per payday (Q1) would be $12,006,613.28 at FY2026’s 95.65; the books show $12,057,194.78, $50,581.50 (0.4%) more. That fits the five individual rate changes and no general raise (Q1, tested in stage 4). Within the threshold.

trail.what: Run the ghost-employee tests on the whole master file and every paycheck

passages.q: Must HANGS Construction Services file Form 940 for 2026?
passages.a: You're subject to FUTA tax in 2026 on the wages you pay employees who aren't farmworkers or household workers if: you paid wages of $1,500 or more in any calendar quarter in 2025 or 2026, or you had one or more employees for at least some part of a day in any 20 or more different weeks in 2025 or 20 or more different weeks in 2026.

passages.q: What are the 2026 FUTA rate, wage base and credit?
passages.a: For 2026, the FUTA tax rate is 6.0%. The tax applies to the first $7,000 you pay to each employee as wages during the year. ... The credit may be as much as 5.4% of FUTA taxable wages. If you're entitled to the maximum 5.4% credit, the FUTA tax rate after credit is 0.6%.

passages.q: Do employees' 401(k) deferrals come off FUTA wages?
passages.a: Elective employee contributions and deferrals to a plan containing a qualified cash or deferred compensation arrangement (401(k)). Generally exempt, but see section 402(g) for limitation. Taxable. Taxable.

passages.q: When is the Q3 2026 Form 941 due?
passages.a: Your Form 941 is due by the last day of the month that follows the end of the quarter. ... 3. July, August, September September 30 October 31 ... If you made timely deposits in full payment of your taxes for the quarter, you may file by the 10th day of the 2nd month that follows the end of the quarter. ... If any due date for filing falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or legal holiday, you may file your return on the next business day.

passages.q: Which employees are counted on line 1, and what goes on lines 2 and 3?
passages.a: Enter the number of employees on your payroll for the pay period including March 12, June 12, September 12, or December 12, for the quarter indicated at the top of Form 941. ... Enter amounts on line 2 that would also be included in box 1 of your employees’ Forms W-2. ... Enter the federal income tax you withheld (or were required to withhold) from your employees on this quarter’s wages, tips, taxable fringe benefits, and supplemental unemployment compensation benefits.

passages.q: Which wages go on line 5a, and where does Social Security stop for each employee?
passages.a: The social security tax rate is 6.2% each for the employee and employer. The social security wage base limit is $184,500. ... For 2026, the rate of social security tax on taxable wages is 6.2% (0.062) each for the employer and employee. Stop paying social security tax on and entering an employee’s wages on line 5a when the employee’s taxable wages and tips reach $184,500 for the year. ... line 5a (column 1) x 0.124 line 5a (column 2)

sources.title: General Instructions for Forms W-2 and W-3 (2026)

passages.q: When are the 2026 Forms W-2 and W-3 due, and must they be e-filed?
passages.a: The due date for filing 2026 Forms W-2 ... and W-3 ... with the SSA is February 1, 2027, whether you file using paper forms or electronically. ... Generally, you must furnish Copies B, C, and 2 of Form W-2 to your employees by February 1, 2027. ... You must e-file Forms W-2 ... if you are required to file at least 10 information returns.

passages.q: What goes in box 1, and are the 401(k) deferrals and Washington Paid Leave premiums in it?
passages.a: Box 1-Wages, tips, other compensation. Show the total taxable wages, tips, and other compensation that you paid to your employee during the year. However, do not include elective deferrals (such as employee contributions to a section 401(k) or 403(b) plan) ... You must include the employee contribution and the employer voluntary payment as wages on the Form W-2.

passages.q: What are the 2026 Social Security limits for boxes 3 and 4, and what goes in boxes 5 and 6?
passages.a: The total of boxes 3 and 7 cannot exceed $184,500 (2026 maximum social security wage base). ... For 2026, the amount should not exceed $11,439 ... there is no wage base limit for Medicare tax ... an employer is required to withhold a 0.9% Additional Medicare Tax on any Federal Insurance Contributions Act (FICA) wages ... in excess of $200,000 in a calendar year.
